speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you describe the exact location of your lower back pain and which specific part of your leg the pain radiates to?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any immediate weakness, numbness, or tingling in your leg or foot at the moment the pain started? Also, does coughing or sneezing make the pain significantly worse?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must respectfully disagree with the previous doctor's assessment, as iron deficiency anemia does not cause radiating nerve pain. To rule out a herniated disc, have you noticed any specific weakness in your foot, such as difficulty lifting your toes or heel? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI confirms an L5-S1 disc herniation, which explains your radiating pain. Do you have any loss of bowel or bladder control, or numbness in the saddle area?

DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Herniated Disc
